Emily —

Appreciate the detail. I reviewed Acme's redlines and we propose the following path forward (high level):

1) Accept the temporary SLO exception (30 days) subject to an explicit Transfer-Impact Addendum that:
   - Defines the exact window and the EU provisioning milestones that trigger termination of the exception;
   - Requires Redwood to enable continuous audit log retention for all cross-border requests for the exception period (minimum 90 days);
   - Mandates Customer-supplied KMS or a customer-specific CMK in Redwood's HSM for the EU cluster once provisioned;

2) SCCs: we will keep the standard SCCs (Controller/Processor) but add a supplementary schedule clarifying responsibilities for export controls and subprocessors in Private deployments;

3) Redline approach: I prepared language that narrows Acme's proposed delegation and introduces the Transfer-Impact Addendum (attached as redline). If that aligns, we can issue a DocuSign packet for the amended DPA.

Quoting Emily's original ask for context:
> "We need explicit language that places responsibility for cross-border transfer decisions on the vendor when Private (customer-hosted) deployments are used."

We can't fully accept an open-ended vendor takeover of transfer decisions, but the Transfer-Impact Addendum can clarify temporary authority limited to provisioning and emergency fallbacks, combined with the audit/KMS mitigations.

I’ve opened a ticket to track formal language and approvals: JIRA: LEG-4129. Draft redline is at: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cDPAredlines (ACME_DPA_REDLINE_v2).

If Acme agrees to the controls above we can get the amended DPA to DocuSign by end of day tomorrow.

Regards,
